_description: Site-wide Open Graph / Twitter Card contract. Confirmed by direct grep across the whole src/ tree: ZERO openGraph or twitter fields exist anywhere in this codebase today (no root-layout default, no per-family override). This file defines the contract to implement, with a real, non-invented fallback hierarchy - it does not implement it (that's a code change beyond this round's contract-only scope for the shared metadata layer, and the per-family images described as NEEDS-DESIGN-ASSET literally don't exist as files yet).
currentState: NOT IMPLEMENTED anywhere. grep -rn "openGraph\|twitter:\|og:image" src/ returns zero matches.
onlyRealImageAssetAvailable: public/portrait.jpg (referenced today only as JsonLd's Person.image) - no purpose-built OG image (1200x630 or similar) exists anywhere in the repo. Every other file under public/ is an unrelated Next.js boilerplate icon (file.svg, globe.svg, next.svg, vercel.svg, window.svg).
fallbackHierarchy: 1. Per-page/per-record image, if a page family is later given one (none exist today - see needsDesignAsset below)

2. Site default OG image - DOES NOT EXIST YET. Until a real 1200x630 asset is designed and committed to public/, og:image should point at public/portrait.jpg rather than a fabricated path - it's the only real asset in the repository, even though its aspect ratio isn't ideal for a social card.

3. No og:image at all is preferable to a broken/404 image URL - if implementing before a real asset exists, omit og:image entirely rather than point at a path that returns 404 (most platforms fall back to their own default preview gracefully; a broken image URL looks worse than none).

fieldsPerFamily.note: og:url and og:type='website' can be set identically everywhere via the same pageAlternates-adjacent mechanism (build og:url from the same canonical string already computed). og:title/og:description should literally reuse the same string already computed for <title>/<meta description> per family - no separate authoring pass needed, since the contracts in seo-title-contract.json and meta-description-contract.json already produce the right values for this purpose.

about.og:type: profile (Open Graph supports this type; alternatively 'website' if simplicity is preferred - a design/product decision, not a technical requirement)

lab-product.og:image: site default, or a per-project image later
lab-product.needsDesignAsset: NEEDS-DESIGN-ASSET for a per-project card (2 instances: ab-testing, dashboard-builder) - not a blocker, site default covers it until then

ab-test-library-detail.og:image: site default - a per-scenario generated card (showing the question + category) would be a genuinely valuable enhancement given the 211-page scale, but that's a template/generator asset, not a one-off design file - NEEDS-DESIGN-ASSET flagged for a reusable OG-image-generation template, not 211 individual images

journey-library-detail.og:image: site default - same reasoning as ab-test-library-detail: a generated per-journey card (id + name + category) is the eventual right answer, not 255 hand-made images

calculator-detail.og:image: site default, or a per-calculator generated card (metric name + example) later
calculator-detail.needsDesignAsset: NEEDS-DESIGN-ASSET for a generated-template card across 43 calculators - not urgent, calculators are typically shared by direct link/embed rather than social card, but flagged for completeness

blog-article.og:image: site default until per-article cover images exist
blog-article.needsDesignAsset: NEEDS-DESIGN-ASSET - only 5 articles today, a per-article cover image is realistic to hand-design at this scale, unlike the 211/255-page corpora above
blog-article.additionalFields: article:published_time from post.date is a real, available field once openGraph.article is implemented

twitterCard.recommendation: twitter:card = 'summary_large_image' site-wide once a real OG image exists (summary_large_image degrades gracefully to a smaller preview if the image is missing/wrong aspect ratio, so it's safe to set even before per-family images exist); twitter:title/twitter:description can mirror og:title/og:description exactly - no separate authoring needed.

implementationNote: This is a contract, not a code change - implementing it means adding an `openGraph`/`twitter` block to the same metadata-builder functions already documented in seo-title-contract.json/meta-description-contract.json (pageAlternates could reasonably grow an `og` sibling function, or each per-family metadata builder could add the block inline). That's plumbing work for the next round; this round's job was confirming there is currently nothing to preserve/break and defining what correct looks like.
